hero.name: Maya Kapoor
hero.intro: Maya is a product designer who turns tangled, high-stakes workflows into calm, usable software. For eight years she has worked with clinical, financial and logistics teams to find the real problem first, then design the smallest thing that solves it.

metadata.title: Maya Kapoor — Product Designer
metadata.description: Maya Kapoor designs calm, usable software for clinical, financial and logistics teams. Selected work, experience and contact.

systems_practice.heading: Clarity first, then craft — in that order.
systems_practice.intro: A short loop of listening, testing and simplifying, repeated until the work is obvious.

pillars.title: Find the real problem
pillars.description: Interviews, shadowing and data before any pixels, so the team agrees what is broken.

pillars.title: Design the smallest thing
pillars.description: Prototype early, test with real users and ship the simplest version that works.

pillars.title: Make it a system
pillars.description: Reusable patterns and clear documentation so the next ten screens take a day.

pillars.title: Stay for the outcome
pillars.description: Work with engineers through launch and measure whether the change helped people.

connect.heading: Let's make something clear.
connect.intro: Open to a small number of product and design-systems engagements each year.

atlas.about_heading: A designer who listens before drawing.
atlas.about_intro: Maya grew up between Mumbai and Zürich and still notices how differently people read the same screen. She leads design for clinical software, mentors a small team, and keeps one day a week for research with the people who use her work.
atlas.about_quote: Good design feels obvious only after someone has done the hard thinking.

experience.description: Leads design for the clinician dashboard used across sixty hospitals.
Designed merchant onboarding and the first shared design system.
Shipped research-led improvements to a logistics planning tool.

projects.title: Clinician dashboard
projects.summary: A calmer home screen for nurses working across dozens of patients.
projects.problem: Nurses lost minutes per patient switching between four screens to find the next task, and critical alerts were buried among routine notices.
projects.approach: We shadowed eighteen nurses across three hospitals, mapped the real handoff moments and rebuilt the dashboard around one prioritised queue with clear alert tiers, prototyping and testing every change on the ward.
projects.outcome: Charting time fell by a third and alert response improved in all three pilot hospitals.

projects.title: Merchant onboarding
projects.summary: A guided setup that took small merchants from signup to first payment.
projects.problem: Small merchants abandoned onboarding when asked for documents they did not have to hand.
projects.approach: We split the flow into saveable steps, explained why each document mattered and let merchants take payments before verification finished.
projects.outcome: Completed signups rose sharply within the first quarter.

projects.title: Shared design system
projects.summary: One component library for four product teams.
projects.problem: Four teams shipped four slightly different buttons, forms and tables.
projects.approach: We audited every pattern, agreed the smallest useful set and documented usage with live examples and accessibility notes.
